claims.statement: All time-driven business work in ECShopX-Java is scheduled through XXL-JOB 2.5.0, with the admin console deployed as a separate container/service (xuxueli/xxl-job-admin:2.5.0) whose scheduling brain (cron expressions, trigger loop, run log, alarm machinery) is outside the Spring application; there is no Quartz and no Spring @Scheduled cron for business jobs.

XxlJobConfig in ecshopx-bootstrap is the entire application-side XXL-JOB integration: it reads eight xxl.job.* properties via @Value and exposes one XxlJobSpringExecutor bean that auto-registers with the admin and receives trigger callbacks on port 19999, with log path logs/xxl-job and 7-day log retention.

The repo-default executor configuration is appname ecshopx-executor, executor port 19999, admin address http://127.0.0.1:9080/xxl-job-admin and accessToken ecshopx-cron-dev; the seeded xxl_job_group row uses app_name ecshopx-executor with address_type 0 (auto-registration), and the accessToken must match the admin's PARAMS token or triggers are rejected.

docker/tables_xxl_job.sql provisions the dedicated xxl_job MySQL schema end to end: it CREATE/USEs the xxl_job database, the eight XXL-JOB tables (xxl_job_info, xxl_job_log, xxl_job_log_report, xxl_job_logglue, xxl_job_registry, xxl_job_group, xxl_job_user, xxl_job_lock), the executor group ecshopx-executor, the console user admin with MD5 password e10adc3949ba59abbe56e057f20f883e (i.e. 123456, role 1), and 69 job definitions for job group 1.

All 69 seeded xxl_job_info jobs are BEAN-mode CRON jobs with executor_route_strategy FIRST, executor_block_strategy SERIAL_EXECUTION, misfire_strategy DO_NOTHING and trigger_status 1, at frequencies from every minute (e.g. cancel-orders) to fixed daily slots (e.g. finish-orders at 03:00); the executor_handler value in each row must equal the @XxlJob short name in code or the handler never fires, because there is no code-side job registration.

The seeded job set is not a guaranteed mirror of the code: ecshopx-promotions' recover-turntable-processing @XxlJob handler exists in code with no corresponding xxl_job_info row in the seed, so it must be created in the admin console before it runs.

The seed SQL only executes on first MySQL initialisation via docker-entrypoint-initdb.d (mounted as 00-tables_xxl_job.sql, before the business 10-ecshopx.sql, in both compose stacks); re-importing requires recreating the volume, and jobs added after initialisation are registered through the admin console rather than through code.

All 72 @XxlJob handler methods across 18 Bundles follow one uniform template: a @Component Schedule*Handler class with a short-name constant used for the @XxlJob value, the [cron][<short-name>] log tags and the CronAlertEvent payload; a parameterless execute() that delegates to a service, logs an INFO done line with cost in ms on success; and on exception logs an ERROR failed line, publishes a CronAlertEvent via ApplicationEventPublisher, then rethrows so XXL-JOB records a failed run.

Cron handlers contain no business logic of their own and use no XXL-JOB API surface — they never use XxlJobHelper or implement IJobHandler, do not shard, and communicate success/failure purely by exception propagation; all real work lives in delegated services (NormalOrderCronService, WechatPayService, TaskService, PagesTemplateServices, etc.).

CronAlertEvent (ecshopx-common/.../common/cron/event) is a plain Spring ApplicationEvent carrying exactly handlerShortName and cause; because it is published through the injected ApplicationEventPublisher, delivery is synchronous, in-process and distinct from dispatch-bus events.

No listener for CronAlertEvent exists anywhere in the repository (no @EventListener or ApplicationListener for it); the event is an alerting seam, not active alerting, and the durable failure signals are the handler ERROR log, XXL-JOB's own xxl_job_log rows and alarm machinery, and the dispatch bus failed_jobs path for handlers that fan out to jobs.

The recurring @XxlJob handler families across bundles are: order lifecycle cancel/finish/consumption and order money (orders: cancel-orders, cancel-offlinepay-orders, cancel-group-orders, finish-orders, consumption-orders, settle-order-profit, share-order-profit, generate-statements, update-rights-status), invoicing (create-invoice, query-invoice, query-invoice-red), ChinaUMS division SFTP file exchange (chinaums-division-transfer/resubmit/download-sftp), after-sales and refunds (aftersales: refuse-aftersales, close-order-item-aftersales, done-aftersales, schedule-refund), promotions/group-buying lifecycle (fail-group, done-group, done-nostore-group, trigger/invalid-promotion-activity, expire-specific-crowd-discount, expire-crowd-month, clear-turntable-times-over), statistics/data cubes (data-cube, companys, hfpay daily-statistics and record-* families), payment channel status and money movement (payment/adapay/hfpay: wechat-query-merchant-payment, adapay/bspay-confirm-retry, adapay-get-submit-license-audit, adapy-draw-cash-queue, hypay-check-cash, hypay-distributor-withdraw), Aliyun SMS (aliyunsms-query-sign/template-audit-status, aliyunsms-query-sms-send-detail, aliyunsms-update-task, aliyunsms-run-task), points/coupons/engagement/theming (send-member-point, settle-brokerage, cancel-expired-card, finish-community-activity, send-wx-remind-msg, enable-theme-template), file hygiene (espier: delete-error-file, delete-history-file), ERP sync (system-link: sync-wdt-logistics, sync-wdt-inventory), and analytics upload (youshu: youshu-order-sum, youshu-add-wxapp-visit-page/distribution).

Cron handlers come in two shapes. Queue-feeders publish one dispatch-bus job per tick and return a fixed 1: finish-orders publishes FINISH_ORDER_JOB via FinishOrderJobDispatchPublisherImpl as ASYNC/REDIS/queue slow, consumption-orders publishes CONSUMPTION_ORDER_JOB on slow with payload orderType=normal pageSize=100, send-member-point dispatches SEND_MEMBER_POINT_JOB on slow, and schedule-refund publishes one REFUND_JOB per AUDIT_SUCCESS refund with staggered delays (0 s for the first refund of an order, 60*n+1 s for repeats) to spread the refund spike.

Direct-worker cron handlers execute the batch inline in the trigger call: NormalOrderCronService.scheduleCancelOrders counts expired NOTPAY orders (auto_cancel_time within 60 s, excluding offline_pay and point pay types), then pages through them 20 at a time (PAGE_SIZE = 20) batch-updating main and association orders to CANCEL and, per order, running the restore fan-out (invoice cancellation, supplier-order cancellation, marketing join-count decrement, points/upoints return, process logs via OrderProcessLogPublishPort, an after-commit marketing dispatch event, employee-purchase restore, per-item inventory and purchase-limit restores, limited-time-sale quota restores, coupon/directed-promotion restore), returning the cancelled count that ends up in the handler INFO log.

NormalOrderCronService.scheduleConsumptionOrders is skipped under the OEM (Shuyun) flag ecshopx.request-field.oem-shuyun=true — it logs and returns 0 without publishing; otherwise it publishes the consumption job on the slow queue.

The queue-feeder publisher implementations in bootstrap are annotated @Profile("!test-cron") (FinishOrderJobDispatchPublisherImpl, ConsumptionOrderJobDispatchPublisherImpl, AftersalesRefundJobDispatchPublisherImpl), and each cron-owning bundle ships a cron/testcfg/CronTestMockConfig annotated @Profile("test-cron") living in src/main that installs @Bean @Primary No-op replacements for the dispatch publishers and side-effect ports, so cron runs during PHP-to-Java schema-diff comparison do not write Redis, call third parties or enqueue real bus jobs.

xxl.job.* properties are case-sensitive and therefore injected Spring-Boot-CLI style via the APP_ARGS environment variable in Docker: docker/app-entrypoint.sh appends APP_ARGS verbatim to the java command (java $JAVA_OPTS -jar $JAR $APP_ARGS), and both compose stacks pass --xxl.job.admin.addresses, --xxl.job.accessToken, --xxl.job.executor.appname and --xxl.job.executor.port through APP_ARGS; the readme states this preserves the semantics of case-sensitive properties such as xxl.job.accessToken.

The admin URL differs per environment: the repo default in application.properties is http://127.0.0.1:9080/xxl-job-admin for self-hosted runs, while both compose stacks override it via APP_ARGS to http://xxl-job-admin:8080/xxl-job-admin on the shared bridge network with the admin's host port published as 8080 (overridable via XXL_HOST_PORT, exposed as --xxl-port by dev-setup.sh and docker-lite/deploy.sh); in both stacks the ecshopx-app service depends_on xxl-job-admin with condition service_healthy (TCP check on 8080, 90 s start period).

Spring @Scheduled exists only for infrastructure polls, enabled by four @EnableScheduling configs — OrdersSchedulingConfig, DoumenIntlPaymentSchedulingConfig (payment), SelfserviceSchedulingConfig and ShuyunOpenPlatformConfiguration — which drive the dispatch-queue pollers, a community-activity cancel queue poller and token-refresh watermarks (DoumenIntlTokenRefreshScheduler, @Scheduled(cron = "0 * * * * ?")); removing those bundles stops the dispatch queues draining but affects no XXL-JOB handler, and vice versa.

A cron-owning bundle needs com.xuxueli:xxl-job-core 2.5.0 on its compile classpath: most cron-owning bundles declare it directly in their POM (orders, payment, aftersales, adapay, aliyunsms, community, companys, data-cube, espier, hfpay, kaquan, point, popularize, selfservice, system-link, theme, plus bootstrap), while promotions and youshu currently get it transitively through peer dependencies.

Each handler ships with a mirror Mockito test class (e.g. orders/cron/ScheduleFinishOrdersHandlerTest, payment/cron/ScheduleQueryMerchantPaymentHandlerTest) that pins the template contract using a Logback ListAppender: on success the service method is called once, no CronAlertEvent is published, and an INFO log contains the handler short name, the returned count and the cost; on failure execute() rethrows, exactly one CronAlertEvent is captured with handlerShortName equal to the short name, and an ERROR log contains the short name and failed.

Bootstrap publisher-impl tests (e.g. ConsumptionOrderJobDispatchPublisherImplTest) pin the exact dispatch tuple of the queue-feeder path — message name OrdersDispatchJobNames.CONSUMPTION_ORDER_JOB, ASYNC mode, REDIS driver, queue slow, null delay, platform default retry — plus the null-payload guard that throws IllegalArgumentException.
